features.summary: Run daily generation, bounded AI repair, validation, publication, and terminal summary ownership through one production entrypoint.
commands: corepack pnpm run daily:codex-pipeline -- --date YYYY-MM-DD --execute --publish --codex-bin codex.cmd
acceptance: A needs_ai_repair handoff is preflighted for kind, clean-root evidence realpaths, and direct launcher .tmp destination before Codex authors a contract and the same entrypoint resumes.
Automated repair is capped at five attempts and records attempted, authored, completed, edit count, terminal reason, and explicit failure state without treating a later block as recovery.
Production repair uses read-only schema-constrained UTF-8 Codex output; the host validates and writes the contract, and a bounded timeout terminates the process tree with codex_timeout.
Claim verification overrides misleading source-level inference, quality and report_write share complete candidate coverage, and terminal summaries identify only the latest unresolved failure.

Production Source Watch is connected only when the producer stage returns the exact artifact path/SHA-256 receipt, the dated producer and candidate pool have identical target_id:snapshot_fingerprint sets, and build proves the exact pool path plus SHA-256; zero inclusion remains a valid consumed state.
A live scheduler that still forces not_connected or consumed:false fails the workflow compatibility gate before release.

The project scheduler inventory contains exactly one automation, ai-2; its prompt delegates health truth to the dated run summary, while status:self-check remains a manual diagnostic rather than a second scheduled workflow.
stop_conditions: The entrypoint returns needs_ai_repair without exhausting or disabling its declared repair budget.
Codex writes outside the bounded pipeline work directory.
A requested Source Watch path is reported as consumed without producer, fingerprint-lineage, persisted-pool, and build evidence.
The live automation prompt contradicts evidence-backed Source Watch summary semantics.
Any second D:\ai-daily-cn automation definition or publisher appears beside ai-2.
features.behavior: Keep the automation prompt thin while the repository-owned entrypoint closes repair/resume and terminal-state transitions.

commands: node --test --test-name-pattern "report:draft.*main stream|report:write allows disclosed low-risk refill|quality review.*candidate|quality review shares" tests/unit.test.js

stop_conditions: Repair loops are unbounded or silent.
Source Watch fixture coverage is presented as production connectivity.

features.summary: Track ai-daily recovery work through one stable REC issue ledger and five-layer completion evidence.
commands: node --test --test-name-pattern "project recovery uses one tracked five-layer issue ledger" tests/unit.test.js
acceptance: Every recovery issue has a stable REC ID, fact evidence, state, concrete action, and acceptance or explicit terminal decision; implementing issues also record validation/runtime boundaries.
Closed issues prove implementation, production wiring, automated tests, browser or real scheduled acceptance, and synchronized docs, feature state, generated artifacts, and Handoff.
The ledger preserves lost-source replacements/retirements, half-landed features, design conflicts, confirmed surviving value, and every issue/action discovered in this session.
Later recovery sessions update this ledger instead of creating another broad review or issue list.
stop_conditions: A recovery issue is called closed while any of the five evidence layers is missing.
A second durable recovery issue list is introduced.
Chat memory, TODO text, fixtures, mocks, or uncommitted files are used as closure evidence.
features.behavior: Keep recovery state durable, uniquely identified, and evidence-backed across sessions and PR slices.

commands: node --test --test-name-pattern "project recovery uses one tracked five-layer issue ledger" tests/unit.test.js

stop_conditions: Stable REC IDs or five-layer completion markers drift out of the ledger.
Feature and Harness state disagree with the ledger.

features.summary: Collect and audit daily AI sources before writing the structured report.
commands: corepack pnpm run discover:github-trending -- --date YYYY-MM-DD --limit 50 --history-root reports-data
corepack pnpm run discover:github-watch -- --date YYYY-MM-DD --config config/source-watchlist.json
acceptance: Candidate sources record successful, failed, and empty checks.
Selected items point back to candidate IDs.
Freshness, duplicate URL, and source-window decisions are recorded before report writing.
Per-source parsed_recent uses only that source's parsed_count or recent_48h_entries; group candidate totals never create per-source success.
Phase5 joins final report candidate backrefs, applies the shared source-admission decision, and reports concrete violations, trusted-target upgrades, orphan included flags, and missing backrefs.
Logical-source promotion is evidence-decided per collection entry; defer and retire decisions remain collection-only and never raise source authority.

Source Watch suppresses a target when any material GitHub endpoint fails, selects the newest release or commit event, persists the source snapshot fingerprint, and returns a stage-bound artifact path/hash receipt.

Official-blog daily context reuses existing reviewed knowledge, preserves official-blog-admission-v1, verifies wrapper/source dates plus source/context/bindings hashes and relationships, chooses the highest-score type binding, and never auto-writes curated knowledge.

HTML-index title, summary, and image facts come only from the exact anchor or same-URL structured metadata; adjacent cards cannot trigger high-specificity model-launch topics or prose through evidence text.
stop_conditions: Required source audit fields cannot be reconstructed.
The draft would bypass candidate-pool or freshness gates.
features.behavior: Collect and audit daily AI sources before writing the structured report.

features.summary: Projectize taste-skill and Impeccable as ADC frontend design-read, audit, and browser-acceptance quality gates.
acceptance: Taste-skill is adopted through the local design-taste-frontend skill with its dashboard and data-table boundary preserved.
Impeccable is adopted as optional external design audit evidence, not as a production runtime or CI network dependency.
Material frontend PRs record design read, visual dials, source/tool evidence, audit or skip reason, and browser acceptance.

The React homepage, static shells, and every historical daily report consume one ADC paper/ink visual contract; reports reference the shared generated assets/adc-theme.css instead of embedding a duplicate theme overlay, and sampled desktop plus narrow viewports pass overflow and computed-color checks.
Replacement builds preserve the official-blog home entry and Source Watch article presentation while the retired public-search UI does not return.
Source Watch headings remain visibly paper-colored on the ink panel at desktop and 390px viewports, with an automated CSS contrast contract preventing black-on-black regressions.
The page gate rejects retired model/project sections by exact section label or structural selector without blocking legitimate news-card titles that merely mention model releases.
stop_conditions: Generated or external UI code is committed directly into production paths.
A dense ADC data-product surface is replaced by a landing-page template.
External design tools become unpinned production or CI dependencies without a migration record.

worktree_policy.write_task_isolation: Use one git worktree or branch per write task.
worktree_policy.code_organization: Keep source code organized by project architecture, not by agent task folders.

P0: web browser acceptance when Web user-visible behavior changes
P1: affected module, integration, system, API, data-flow, or cross-boundary checks
risk assessment when a P1 check is skipped
P2: broader regression, repeated runs, cross-browser or mobile viewport, accessibility, or performance hardening
explicit defer reason when not run

required_evidence: screenshot, trace, video, log, or explicit skip reason
web_acceptance_policy.default_tool_boundary: Use webapp-testing for one-off local acceptance; use e2e-testing only for durable Playwright suites.
web_acceptance_policy.safety_boundary: Do not use production accounts, real payments, or external writes unless explicitly approved.

actionable_resolution: fix failing checks that are within the accepted task scope
stop_conditions: user decision
credential or permission boundary
reviewer action
protected-branch override
external service recovery
pr_closeout_policy.merge_boundary: Do not merge a PR unless the user explicitly requests that remote mutation.

required_checks: final independent review or explicit skip reason
technical debt and first-principles implementation fit
PR or merge-readiness status when a PR exists
conflict decisions and risk surfaced to the user
insight audit recommendations or explicit skip reason
finish_closeout_policy.subagent_boundary: Use subagents only for independent read-only review or verification; the main agent owns synthesis and final decisions.
finish_closeout_policy.insight_boundary: Use insight to audit tool calling, repeated low-value lookup loops, misleading evidence, docs/code conflicts, AI infrastructure lessons, and skill or workflow extraction candidates.
finish_closeout_policy.merge_boundary: Drive to merge-ready or complete the merge only when the user explicitly authorizes that remote mutation.

agentic_loop_policy.loop_model: Producer -> Verifier -> Arbiter -> Main Agent Decision
required_evidence: verifier evidence or explicit skip reason
arbiter verdict or explicit skip reason
stop condition when a loop may repeat or iteration controls are recorded
iteration and maxIterations when a loop may repeat

rules: single-pass loops may omit iteration, maxIterations, and stopCondition
when either iteration field is present, both values must be positive integers and stopCondition is required
iteration must be less than or equal to maxIterations
allowed stopCondition values are continue, revise, interrupt, deliver, handoff, and complete

agentic_loop_policy.arbiter_boundary: Arbiters are read-only. They do not edit code, resolve conflicts, push, publish, merge, or make final user-facing decisions.
agentic_loop_policy.dispatch_boundary: Hooks and deterministic checks may request or validate loop evidence, but must not auto-dispatch delegated agents.
agentic_loop_policy.main_agent_responsibility: The main agent owns synthesis, user-visible decisions, integration, and final handoff.

loop_control_policy.control_plane: Loop Engineering decides when to continue, validate, interrupt, and record auditable action decisions.
loop_control_policy.default_behavior: Continue low-risk local work when scope, ownership, and validation are clear; interrupt when risk signals require human review.

context_engineering_policy.knowledge_layer: LLM Wiki keeps stable project knowledge in Markdown without duplicating raw sources or agent-native memory.
context_engineering_policy.write_policy: Initialize incrementally; require human confirmation before knowledge writes; preserve wiki content file-by-file during standard updates.
